“We’ve never been hacked” is going to become a much weaker argument for trusting a crypto company.

AI can already help find vulnerabilities that went unnoticed before. It won’t make every system easy to exploit, but it can make finding and testing weaknesses faster.

That should worry any exchange or company that has been getting away with bare-minimum security.

An old audit and a clean track record aren’t enough. Code changes, employee devices get compromised, permissions pile up. Security has to be tested continuously, including how much damage one compromised account can do.

Defenders have access to AI too. Use it to find the gaps, fix them and tighten access before someone else does.

If you custody user funds, your security budget needs to reflect what an attacker can do today.

“We were safe until yesterday” won’t mean much to someone whose savings are gone.

If you told me before, how much I would think the market would drop if Binance would be hacked and $6 bn stolen, I would say 15-20%. The fact that it found its low at $76,400 shows how strong Bitcoin really is, reacting to such a large hack in such a small decline, and yet the panic of short term holders reached extreme high volume, and even the CoinBase premium reached levels, last seen at the bottom of 2022 during the FTX crash.

As per on-chain data 36,600 BTC from short term holder were sent to exchanges below their purchase cost within 24 hours. The seven-day total of short-term-holder deposits into Binance reached approximately 45,400 BTC. These are deposits of underwater coins, and many already sold in a loss. The amount of realized loss is $1.115 billion in losses over 24 hours which is very high compared to a normal market, and this shows that the exchange deposits, the realized loss happened in very high volumes, and this is how markets react at a black swan or a newly formed bottom. On top, the daily RSI reading was around 34.7, its lowest since June 30, the moment BTC found its bottom at 57k. On October 29, Bitcoin also closed below its lower daily Bollinger Band, another indicator of a big sell-off and not a normal or comfortable pullback, or correction. 

The Coinbase Premium at 0.27% reached its lowest since November 2022, bringing the indicator back into the territory seen during the FTX crisis. That means the discount became deeper than during this year’s earlier sell-off. Usually, the CoinBase Premium is a great indicator that shows us shocks, or Black Swan reactions, and reaching certain Black Swan levels such as the FTX crash, is just another indicator that supports my point that this was indeed a Black Swan and should be considered as one.

The market is reacting with pure emotion. The BTC sent to exchanges during the hack tells that holders are selling into the panic, potentially accepting losses just to get out.  The Fear & Greed Index shows FEAR, but in my view, many inexperienced investors missed the bottom. My assessment is that a larger share of the remaining holders are experienced investors who have already survived a lot of  corrections and crashes. These are people who know how this market works, and even they are feeling the pressure, thats why its on FEAR now, and This is why I interpret the current sentiment as closer to EXTREME FEAR, due to the lack of non experienced investors in the market right now.

Now to my position, because this needs to be understood correctly. My average long entry is $80,400. Bitcoin subsequently traded toward $85K, approximately $4,600 above my entry, has now moved back toward $78K, approximately $2,400 below it. The $80K–$81K support did not hold, and the daily EMA50 and MA50 have been lost. However, the most important level in my opinion is $76,000.  Let us speak about the three levels on the chart, because right now they matter MOST:

Level 1 is the most important level of all, and in my view it is the level that 100% needs to hold. This is the $76K area. Why is it so important? First, because this was the area that confirmed the breakout into the bull market structure. Second, because it is very close to the major weekly support region and at the 50 Weekly Moving Average, which makes it a zone many bigger players will watch. Third, because it is also around the area where a lot of recent buyers, short-term holders and stronger hands are sitting with their cost basis. And fourth, because after the black swan event, this was the zone where the market found a reaction and stopped the panic. The area of 76k is the structure that keeps the bull market alive. The outcome of losing 76k will be brutal, It would open a much more serious downside scenario, with $67K–$69K becoming a risk, but I stay relaxed as long 76k holds. To confirm a loss of 76k it requires at least 2-3 days of closed daily candles below it. 

Level 2 is the next area I am watching very closely. This is the level that, once broken and then reclaimed, would be a very strong signal for the bulls. Why? Because it would show that the market has absorbed the panic selling from the hack, that the shakeout is over, and that buyers are taking back control. In other words, Level 2 is the first signal that things are returning back to normality. It would tell me that the market is no longer simply bouncing weakly from the lows, but that it is starting to rebuild strength again. This is why I want to see not only a touch of that level, but a proper reclaim with daily closes above. 

Then we have Level 3, which is around $82K. This is the level I have spoken about many times in the past. The $80K–$81K area was support, and now after the black swan event we do not want to see that whole region turning into resistance. We need to reclaim it as support again. Once the market gets back above the $80K–$81K zone, I believe the $82K breakout will happen almost by itself, because that is the point where the structure becomes clearly bullish again and where the market would show that the panic was only a shakeout. I have said many times that $82K was one of the most important breakout levels for the start of the bull market, and that does not change now. Regaining that area would be a very strong statement by the bulls and this is exactly what is required now by the market. The longer we take in the current region, and not reclaiming 82k, the more bears will gain more power as a recovery should happen quick in my opinion.

As per Calendar this Week is very hot as well, Apple, Palantir, AMD report earnings this week on Today and Tuesday. On top we have the mid terms on Tuesday as well. Expect a lot of volatility this Week! 

I remain confident in the bull-market continuation scenario, provided $76K holds. My longs at an average of $80,400 remain open, alongside the spot positions I began building at $60,000.

Security risks (AI-driven hacks, mathematical breakthroughs & quantum computing) have become increasingly concerning in recent weeks both personally & for the broader market. 

$ZEC looks like the best way to play this, and the market is already showing us that with clear divergence vs BTC/ETH/SOL/HYPE/TOTAL3ES over the past couple weeks.

Additionally, short-term spot & derivatives positioning looks significantly cleaner vs earlier this month. ETF flows have just flipped positive again after ~3 weeks of outflows, while coin-denominated OI is at its lowest level since August.

Separately, OTC desks are still seeing strong interest from liquid & VC funds, with ZEC reportedly remaining one of the most bought altcoins by funds even at these elevated prices.

I generally view protocol upgrades as weak catalysts in isolation, but the January upgrade feels different. Tachyon addresses the scalability improvements the community has been waiting for, while the quantum component of the upgrade addresses one of the highest mindshare risks to the industry. Together, I think they make for a much stronger catalyst than either would on its own.

The combination of improving positioning, continued institutional demand, relative strength & an increasingly powerful narrative makes for an attractive setup, even in shaky market conditions. I expect my conviction to continue building as we approach January.

I have no strong view on market direction over the coming months, and the quantum tailwind for ZEC is a headwind for BTC, so I’m hedged vs BTC on a vol-adjusted basis, but think a naked long is also justified.

Quantum is the crypto equivalent of cancer and ZEC is the cure. Don’t find yourself Zidelined on the road past $2k

My thoughts on the market and $BTC after the record breaking Binance hack 👇

$BTC has come down and filled this inefficiency, it tapped right at the Daily 200EMA & Top of the Bull market support band.

Up on a break of $80K, this was the top of my price range where I'd get interested again for long term value. I would expect BTC to hold its ground between here and $72K-$73K (which is close from here anyways).

If this was it, price recovers back above $80K and everything looks solid again, then that would be a sign of strength for me. These Daily 200EMA & Bull Market support band retests do pretty much always occur when a bear market transitions into a new bull market. They always look scary. This was the largest drawdown since the $58K-$87K rally. But still only -12% so nothing to go crazy over.

From my memory these post hack markets do tend to be somewhat choppy and take some time to recover usually. Especially because trust and sentiment take a big hit. That is a good recipe for a (local) bottom eventually, but it generally takes some time to play out.

We will see the occasional headlines on when the hacker is moving/selling BTC & ETH and might see some weakness on that news when it occurs. But the amounts are nothing the market would lose its sleep over at the current size of the market.

Low timeframe I am looking for a retest to the .786 fib level around ~$76.9K to see if that makes one of those marginally higher lows and then bounces. Those have been pretty reliable after big moves and retests for $BTC the past few years. If not, we patiently wait and see what happens.

This event was nowhere close to the damage something like the 10/10 market crash or whatever comparison some people are making. Different market environments as well so hard to compare these things.

Let the market and charts lead.

So to summarize: 
- Bitcoin at the top of the high timeframe value zone already. I like long term spot buys between here and $72K.
- Daily 200EMA & Bull Market support band retests are normal when transitioning in a new high timeframe uptrend.
- Hack not as bad or comparable as 10/10 imo
- Nothing changes for alts vs BTC specifically for me here. Some alts sold off more than others because of the hacked amount but have also retraced that already. Don't think there's any edge there specifically. Just need to remain selective as always.

My thoughts on the market and $BTC after the record breaking Binance hack 👇

$BTC has come down and filled this inefficiency, it tapped right at the Daily 200EMA & Top of the Bull market support band.

Up on a break of $80K, this was the top of my price range where I'd get interested again for long term value. I would expect BTC to hold its ground between here and $72K-$73K (which is close from here anyways).

If this was it, price recovers back above $80K and everything looks solid again, then that would be a sign of strength for me. These Daily 200EMA & Bull Market support band retests do pretty much always occur when a bear market transitions into a new bull market. They always look scary. This was the largest drawdown since the $58K-$87K rally. But still only -12% so nothing to go crazy over.
